The best universities for Hospitality Management in UK for 2027 include the University of Surrey, Oxford Brookes University, Bournemouth University, Ulster University and Leeds Beckett University.

Surrey is the strongest overall choice in this comparison. Oxford Brookes offers an attractive balance of subject reputation, placement opportunities and cost, while Bournemouth is particularly strong if you want hospitality and tourism in the same degree.

There is an important difference between the courses, though. Some universities teach dedicated Hospitality or Hotel Management degrees. Others combine hospitality with tourism or business. For a student targeting hotel operations, revenue management, food and beverage or guest experience, that distinction can matter more than a few places in a league table.

Hospitality University Ranking UK: How This List Was Built

A hospitality university ranking UK comparison becomes misleading if it relies on one league table alone.

QS measures Hospitality and Leisure Management internationally. The Guardian uses a different UK methodology, while official course pages tell you something rankings cannot: whether the degree actually covers hospitality operations, placements, revenue management, tourism or broader business.

For this comparison, hospitality-specific academic standing carries the most weight, followed by course relevance and placement opportunities. International fees and practical value also matter.

That produces a different answer from simply copying QS.

For example, Ulster and Leeds Beckett gain ground because their current hospitality provision combines strong UK subject signals with practical programmes and substantially lower published fees than Surrey.

1. University of Surrey

Surrey takes first place because it combines the strongest hospitality-specific ranking in this list with a dedicated degree and established professional training.

It ranks 18th globally and 1st in the UK for Hospitality and Leisure Management in QS 2026. Surrey also reports first place in the UK for tourism, transport, travel and heritage in the Complete University Guide 2027.

Its International Hospitality Management BSc covers core management alongside hospitality operations and offers a Professional Training route. The latest confirmed overseas fee is £22,900 for 2026/27, while the 2027 fee remains to be confirmed.

The trade-off is simple: Surrey costs more than several alternatives, but the premium buys unusually strong subject visibility and a clear hospitality identity.

Best for: reputation, specialist hospitality study and placement.

2. Oxford Brookes University

Oxford Brookes is the strongest value challenger to Surrey.

Its Hospitality and Leisure Management subjects rank 29th globally and 2nd in the UK in QS 2026.

The university's International Hospitality and Tourism Management degree combines hospitality with tourism and offers placement opportunities. More importantly for 2027 applicants, the published international fee is £18,500 for 2027/28.

At current published figures, that is £4,400 below Surrey's latest confirmed annual fee.

That does not make Oxford Brookes automatically better, but it makes the value comparison much more interesting.

If English eligibility could change your shortlist, check how UK universities assess English-language evidence before applying.

Best for: strong subject reputation at a lower published cost than Surrey.

3. Bournemouth University

Bournemouth works particularly well for students who see hospitality and tourism as connected industries.

Hospitality and Leisure Management ranks 30th globally in QS 2026 at Bournemouth.

Its International Tourism and Hospitality Management BA is available for 2027 entry. The latest published international fee is £19,635 for the September 2026 start, and the university lists IELTS 6.0 overall with at least 5.5 in each component for 2026 and 2027 entry.

Bournemouth also has a practical location advantage. Hotels, restaurants, attractions and tourism businesses form part of the local economy, not just case studies in a lecture.

Students leaning more towards live experiences and events can naturally compare degrees built around event management careers.

Best for: hospitality, tourism and destination management.

4. Ulster University

Ulster is one of the strongest specialist alternatives outside the usual Surrey, Oxford Brookes and Bournemouth conversation.

Its 2027/28 International Hospitality Management BSc is a dedicated hospitality degree, and Ulster reports 3rd place in the UK for Hospitality, Event Management and Tourism in the Guardian University Guide 2026.

The 2027/28 fee is not yet published. The comparable 2026/27 full-time international cost is £17,490 for 120 credits.

The appeal here is practical. Students get a clear hospitality programme without paying the tuition associated with some higher-profile institutions.

Best for: dedicated hospitality study and practical value.

5. Leeds Beckett University

Leeds Beckett is the most convincing lower-fee option in this Top 10.

Its Hospitality Business Management BSc costs £16,840 for international students in 2026/27, with a reduced placement-year fee of £2,526.

The university ranks 4th in the UK for Hospitality, Event Management and Tourism in the Guardian University Guide 2026, and its hospitality course highlights links with the Leeds Hotels & Venues Association.

Here's the mildly surprising part: the cheapest published tuition in this comparison sits alongside one of the stronger UK subject positions.

That is why students looking for hotel management in UK with low fees should compare course quality rather than assuming cheaper means weaker.

For a broader budget check, compare UK universities with lower international tuition.

Best for: cost, hospitality business and industry exposure.

6. University of Derby

Derby offers a dedicated International Hospitality Management BA and keeps the programme close to industry practice.

The course is recognised within a subject area ranked Top 25 for Hospitality, Event Management and Tourism in the Guardian University Guide 2026.

International tuition is £17,500 per year for 2026/27 after the foundation stage, where applicable.

Derby makes sense for students who want a specialist hospitality title but cannot justify tuition above £20,000.

Best for: practical hospitality management at a moderate fee.

7. University of Westminster

Westminster is the clearest choice here for students specifically searching for a hotel-focused degree.

Its International Hotel Management BA starts in September 2027, costs £19,000 per year for international students, and is taught at Marylebone in central London.

Unlike broader tourism and hospitality programmes, the degree is explicitly centred on international hotel management.

London gives students access to one of the UK's deepest hotel and hospitality markets, although living costs can be considerably higher.

Students committed to the capital can also compare other London universities for international students.

Best for: dedicated hotel management and London industry exposure.

8. Sheffield Hallam University

Sheffield Hallam is better suited to students who want hospitality with broader business skills.

Its Business Management and Hospitality BA starts in September 2027, costs £18,900 per year for international students, and includes a placement-year option.

The programme combines hospitality operations with strategy, leadership and consultancy.

That makes it less specialist than Surrey, Ulster or Derby, but potentially more flexible for a student who may later move into management or business development.

Best for: hospitality plus business and work experience.

9. University of Strathclyde

Strathclyde approaches hospitality through a business-school lens.

Its Hospitality and Tourism Management pathway combines the sector with wider management study, while the current international fee is £22,750 per year.

This is not the obvious choice for someone who wants a narrowly operational hotel degree. It is more compelling for students interested in tourism strategy, service management, marketing or consultancy.

Best for: broader commercial and management mobility.

10. Manchester Metropolitan University

Manchester Metropolitan combines hospitality and tourism with business management in a major UK city.

Its International Hospitality and Tourism Business Management BSc has a published overseas fee of £20,000 per year.

Manchester itself adds context: hotels, conferences, restaurants, sport, music and major events create year-round demand across the visitor economy.

The university also reports an institution-wide Graduate Outcomes figure of 87.6% of UK-domiciled full-time first-degree graduates in employment or further study after 15 months. That figure is not hospitality-specific.

Best for: hospitality business in a large city.

Surrey, Ulster and Derby offer dedicated hospitality degrees. Westminster is even more hotel-specific. Oxford Brookes and Bournemouth combine hospitality with tourism, while Leeds Beckett and Sheffield Hallam bring more business into the programme.

Most undergraduate routes take three years, with many adding an optional placement or sandwich year.

If the application system is unfamiliar, understanding how international students use UCAS is useful before you start comparing deadlines and offers.

Best Hotel Management Courses in UK for International Students

Students searching for hotel management courses in UK for international students often find Hospitality Management degrees in the same results.

The terms overlap, but the course focus can differ.

Hotel management usually concentrates on hotel operations, front office, rooms, food and beverage, revenue and guest services. Hospitality management is broader and can extend into resorts, restaurants, tourism, events, luxury services and customer experience.

For hotel management courses UK, Westminster offers the clearest hotel-specific undergraduate title in this list. Surrey provides the strongest overall hospitality profile. Ulster and Derby offer practical dedicated hospitality alternatives.

For broader hospitality courses in UK for international students, Oxford Brookes, Bournemouth and Leeds Beckett widen the route into tourism or business.

The course title is useful. The modules matter more.

Scholarships can also change the net price. Oxford Brookes currently advertises a £2,000 International Student Scholarship for eligible September 2026 entrants, while Leeds Beckett states that international scholarship support can range from £1,000 to £6,000, depending on the award and eligibility.

Because awards change by intake, compare current UK scholarship opportunities once you have narrowed the university list.

Entry Requirements and Placement Experience

Entry requirements vary by university and applicant country, but many undergraduate hospitality programmes ask for English at around IELTS 6.0 overall with no component below 5.5. Bournemouth and Sheffield Hallam both publish that level for the courses covered here.

At postgraduate level, a recognised bachelor's degree is normally required. Some programmes accept graduates from different academic backgrounds, while specialist hotel-management courses may expect relevant study or experience.

Placement deserves real weight in the decision.

Hospitality is practical. A lecture can explain revenue management or service recovery, but it cannot reproduce a full hotel, an unpredictable guest problem or a busy restaurant service.

That is why professional training at Surrey, sandwich routes at Oxford Brookes, and placement options at Bournemouth, Leeds Beckett and Sheffield Hallam strengthen those courses considerably.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which university is best for Hospitality Management in UK?

The University of Surrey is the strongest overall choice in this comparison. It ranks 1st in the UK and 18th globally for Hospitality and Leisure Management in QS 2026 and offers dedicated hospitality study with Professional Training.

What are the top hospitality universities in UK?

Surrey, Oxford Brookes and Bournemouth lead this list for hospitality-specific academic standing. Ulster and Leeds Beckett are particularly strong alternatives when practical study and cost are given more weight.

What are the best hospitality management courses in UK?

Surrey is strongest for dedicated hospitality management, Westminster for hotel-specific study, Oxford Brookes and Bournemouth for hospitality with tourism, and Leeds Beckett for hospitality business.

Which university offers hotel management in UK with low fees?

Among the universities compared here, Leeds Beckett has the lowest published undergraduate fee at £16,840 for 2026/27. Ulster's comparable figure is £17,490 and Derby's is £17,500.

What are the top universities for masters in hospitality management?

Surrey, Oxford Brookes, Sheffield Hallam and Derby are strong current options. Their programmes cover international hotel management, hospitality and tourism management, with published fees ranging from £17,500 to £20,700 in the figures used here.

Is Hospitality Management the same as Hotel Management?

No. Hotel Management focuses more directly on hotel operations, while Hospitality Management can cover hotels, restaurants, resorts, tourism, events and other service businesses.

Which Hospitality University Is the Best Choice?

The best universities for Hospitality Management in UK solve different problems.

Surrey offers the strongest overall hospitality profile. Oxford Brookes comes surprisingly close when ranking, placement and tuition are considered together. Bournemouth is stronger for hospitality plus tourism. Ulster, Leeds Beckett and Derby offer more budget-conscious routes, while Westminster is the clearest choice for a hotel-specific undergraduate degree in London.

The most useful shortlist is therefore not simply the first three names in a ranking.

Compare course focus, placement, tuition and career direction. Those four factors reveal much more about the value of a hospitality degree than word count, university fame or a league-table position on its own.
